candidate.answerReason: There are 9000 equally likely integers and 5·8·8·7=2240 favorable integers. Their ratio simplifies to 56/225, agreeing with choice B.

methods.label: Choose the odd units digit first
methods.explanation:
There are
\[
9999-1000+1=9000
\]
integers in the stated range, all equally likely. To count the favorable integers, choose the units digit first because it determines whether the number is odd.

The units digit has \(5\) choices: \(1,3,5,7,9\). The thousands digit must be nonzero and different from the units digit, leaving \(8\) choices. The hundreds digit can be any of the \(8\) unused digits, including zero if it is still unused. Finally, the tens digit has \(7\) unused choices.

These choices produce every odd four-digit integer with distinct digits. Each is counted once because its four digits specify exactly one sequence of choices. The number of favorable integers is therefore
\[
5\cdot8\cdot8\cdot7=2240.
\]
Dividing the favorable count by the total count gives
\[
\frac{2240}{9000}=\frac{56}{225}.
\]
The probability is \(\frac{56}{225}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
